full_content: The Division of International Affairs is delighted to announce the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Lovely Professional University (LPU) and Lodz University of Technology (TUL), Poland. This strategic collaboration aims to foster mutual co-operation in key areas such as semester exchange, articulation pathways, joint research, summer/winter programs, and more. Founded in 1945 and located in Lódz, Poland, Lodz University of Technology is one of Poland’s leading technical universities and is widely recognized for its strong focus on engineering, innovation, and applied research. The university has built a solid international reputation for academic excellence and industry-oriented education, particularly in fields such as engineering, information technology, materials science, biotechnology, and management. Ranked among the top universities globally in the QS World University Rankings 2026, TUL is also recognized for its growing internationalization efforts and active student mobility programs across Europe and beyond. If you're interested in exploring joint initiatives or a study abroad opportunity with Lodz University of Technology, please feel free to reach out to the Division of International Affairs at 32-310. full_content: Dear Aspirants, Professional Enhancement means expanding your ability to perform a particular task or progressing in your career by upgrading your skills. No matter the field, skill enhancement is a prerequisite for a successful career. Every industry — from fashion to education — evolves with time, and as a result, our existing skills may become outdated, leading to limited or no professional growth. A person with the right blend of functional, technical, and interpersonal skills is always preferred in a professional environment compared to someone lacking these attributes. Therefore, opportunities to enhance your skills should never be missed. full_content: Dear Students, At LPU, student placement and career readiness remain among our highest priorities. The University continuously strives to provide students with the necessary academic support, industry exposure, and skill enhancement opportunities required for successful placements. As part of this commitment, the academic performance of all first-year UG programme students has been reviewed carefully. It has been observed that students having B+,B,C,D,E grade in CAP 172 , programming methodology, require additional strengthening in programming, which forms a critical foundation for technical competency and future placement opportunities. To support these students in improving their programming proficiency and employability skills, the University is introducing a specialized 6-week Summer Placement Readiness and Employability Enhancement Programme (SPR102), tentatively scheduled from 15 June 2026 to 25 July 2026. The programme will be offered without any academic fee. Students opting for the offline mode will only be required to pay applicable hostel charges. Participation in this programme is mandatory for the identified students. Students may choose either of the following modes: Feature / Component Offline Mode (Supervised On-Campus Learning) Online Mode (Virtual Learning) Learning Mode On-campus supervised learning Online learning through MyClass platform Faculty Guidance Faculty-guided learning and mentorship Online instructor support Daily Classes 2 hours daily theory classes+2 hours daily practical class (Mon-Fri) 4 hrs Online classes (theory +Practical) through MyClass (Mon-Fri) Attendance Requirement Mandatory classroom attendance Online Attendance and Participation. Daily Coding Practice Mandatory 10 LeetCode problems daily Mandatory 10 LeetCode problems daily Weekly Evaluation Minimum 40 LeetCode problems completion Minimum 40 LeetCode problems completion Weekend Usage Saturday & Sunday for pending work Saturday & Sunday for pending work Weekly Performance Weightage 30% of final SPR102 grade 30% of final SPR102 grade Final Evaluation Offline test after reopening of University Offline test after reopening of University Important Instructions . Students are required to submit their preference for Online or Offline mode through the link: https://l1nk.dev/yowskl9 . The last date to submit the preference is 31/05/2026 . Completion and submission of weekly programming assignments is mandatory with course instructors. . Weekly performance carries 30% weightage, while the final offline evaluation test carries 70% weightage. . Necessary study material and video lectures will be provided for academic support. . The final evaluation test is compulsory for all students and will be conducted in offline mode after reopening of the University. . The grade obtained in SPR102 may be considered for grade upgradation in the CAP172 course studied during the first semester. . Students demonstrating unsatisfactory performance in the programme may face restrictions in participation in future placement activities. Students are advised to take this initiative seriously and utilize the programme effectively to strengthen their technical skills and improve future career opportunities. In case of any clarification, or assistance related to the SPR102 Summer Placement Readiness Programme, students may raise an RMS through: UMS Dashboard → RMS → Master Category → Placement (Career Services) → SPR101 Summer Placement Readiness Programme School of Computer Application Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Academic Affairs *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

full_content: Community Development Project aims toward understanding the society related issues/problems and then working towards the solutions to these problems for betterment of the society. Thus, community development project is included as a core course in the curriculum of the students. All students who are required to undergo a community development project (CDP) during June-July 2026 as per their program scheme (tentative list of students is attached as Annexure I) are hereby informed that the students can complete their CDP by choosing any NGO/local organizations involved in community development tasks, allowing physical reporting so that students can work on real-time problems existing in the society. Students are encouraged to pursue community development project (CDP) in their relative filed of study. Important Points: 1. Minimum duration required to complete the community development project should be at least 30 hours or at least 4 weeks. 2. Student must identify/choose an NGO/Organization that qualifies for tax exemption under Section 80G. 3. It is mandatory for students to include day wise “GEO-TAGGED PICTURES” in their final report and presentation demonstrating the live work done by students related to CDP (for 30 hours or for 4 weeks). No Presentation/Report shall be acceptable without “Geo Tagged Pictures”. i.e. Every report should have minimum 6 Geo Tagged pictures. 4. The students are required to obtain the certificate from the NGO/ local organizations involved in community development areas describing the topic and number of hours the student has worked with the NGO/local organization to complete the project. The certificate should be included in the final report, to be eligible for appearing in the ETP. 5. For evaluation parameters and report submission details, kindly go through the guidelines for Community Development Project (Annexure-II). 6. The final ETP viva voce for Community Development Project shall be tentatively scheduled after commencement of classes of Upcoming Autumn Term 26271. The final schedule shall be communicated to students at least 7-10 days prior to the date of ETP evaluation. 7. Lastly all the students are required to submit the name and address of their finalized NGO to the university latest till 15th June 2026 for the verification purpose. For the same soon UMS link shall be shared with all the students via UMS my message. 8. For CSE students refer UMS announcement Mandatory CDP Guidelines for students registered in Summer Placement Readiness and Employability enhancement Program (SPR101) and Python Certification and CDP Opportunity for First Year CSE Students (Students having O, A+, A and B+ grades in Python Programming course INT108 – not registered in Summer Placement Readiness and Employability enhancement Program (SPR101) dated 26/05/2026 for CDP options provided by the university. full_content: Dear Students, Strong programming fundamentals developed in the early stages of the program play a significant role in shaping future placement opportunities. Students are encouraged to continue strengthening their programming skills during the summer break. To support continued skill development, students are advised to undertake the following two components during the summer break, enabling them to simultaneously fulfil their Community Development Programme (CDP) requirements while further strengthening their programming skills: Steps to complete Community Development Programme (CDP): Step 1. Python Certification (Recommended): Students are encouraged to register for and complete a Python certification through Infosys Springboard (Part 1 and Part 2): This certification is available free of cost and is intended to provide structured self-paced learning along with industry-relevant technical exposure. Links are given below: Link 1: https://infyspringboard.us.onwingspan.com/web/en/login (link for registration) Link 2: https://infyspringboard.onwingspan.com/web/en/app/toc/lex_auth_0125409616243425281061_shared/overview Link 3: https://infyspringboard.onwingspan.com/web/en/app/toc/lex_auth_012734003600908288382_shared/overview Details regarding how to register are attached with this communication. Step 2. Python-integrated Community Development Programme (Mandatory CDP – 30 Hours): Python-based Community Development Activities (Mandatory CDP Integration –30 Hours): Students shall complete their 30 hrs mandatory CDP through Python-based community engagement activities, such as: a. Teaching Python programming fundamentals to school students/community learners/Conducting Python-based coding workshops / digital literacy sessions (minimum 30 hrs). b. Develop video lecture series explaining basic topics of Python language in a simplified application-based manner. The lecture should elaborate concepts in such a way that your juniors/users should be able to understand the concept very easily. c. The video lecture series should be uploaded on Youtube/any social media platform and the student should include link as well as screenshots of the same in his/her report. d. The final CDP viva will be Scheduled for the student based on following conditions: i. Submission of Infosys Springboard Certificate (Part 1 and 2) ii. Submission of report based only on Python based community engagement activities (Video lecture series/teaching report). e. Instead of the above-mentioned Python course, the students of Computer Science and Engineering can also to pursue community services related to their field of study, such as conducting Cyber Security Awareness camps, Digital literacy camps, e-waste collection interface, digital inclusion platforms, localised AI-driven solutions, and automated administrative tools such as NGO Management Portals. Such engagement offers multiple advantages: . Strengthens technical understanding through practical application . Improves coding confidence through continuous engagement . Develops mentoring, communication, and leadership capabilities . Builds early experiential learning exposure relevant to future careers It is mandatory for students to include day wise “GEO-TAGGED PICTURES” in their final report and presentation demonstrating the live work done by students related to CDP (for 30 hours or for 4 weeks). No Presentation/Report shall be acceptable without “Geo Tagged Pictures”. i.e. Every report should have minimum 6 Geo Tagged pictures. Important Guidelines: 1. Completion of 30 mandatory CDP hours remains compulsory in the above-explained mode. Before proceeding with community teaching, the Infosys Springboard certification completion is mandatory. 2. Python upskilling is strongly recommended as a placement preparedness initiative. 3. All CDP activities must be properly documented as per university norms. Participation in this initiative will help students maintain technical momentum and prepare for more advanced programming expectations in upcoming semesters. In case of any query, students may log an RMS request via the below mentioned path: UMS Navigation---->Relationship Management System (RMS) --->Log Request Message Type: Enquiry Category Type: Academic and Administrative Issues Category: Examination Sub-Category: Seating Plan and VIVA- Capstone/ Dissertation/ Thesis/ CDP/ Summer Training Attachment: 1 Infosys springboard.doc Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Academic Affairs *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

full_content: Admission Referral – National Students (Under Student Revenue Generation Policy – EDU Revolu Hurry up! As part of the University’s Education Revolution (EDU Revolution) and the Student Revenue Generation Policy, Lovely Professional University continues to empower students to become active contributors in the institution’s growth journey. Students can now refer eligible and high-achieving national candidates for admission and earn points under the structured Revenue Generation framework. Students are advised to refer to the official announcement titled “Updated Student Admission Referral Incentives of Student Revenue Generation Policy (Under EDU Revolution)” (Ref. Guidelines (Mandatory) - The referral in all cases must be new and should not exist in any university system before submission. - Only the first verified and portal-submitted referral will be considered valid. - No referral benefit will be given for referring any existing LPU student (joining again with/without completing previous degree). - All referrals must be submitted through the official university portal only. - University holds final discretion on approval of referral and allocation of points. - Points will be reviewed and awards will be granted based on total accumulated points by November 2026. Referral Policy is not applicable in the following cases: - Admission for Online or Distance Mode programmes. - Referring student who is receiving a 100% scholarship. - An existing student (joining again with/without completing previous degree). - Candidate who has already applied for admission before submission of the referral form. - If the referred student’s admission status is not active. full_content: Centre for Professional Enhancement in collaboration with School of Computer Science and Engineering is going to conduct “Aptitude booster -A Webinar based on Quant and logical reasoning”. The event emphasizes on giving students a platform to discuss various kind of Competitive Exam based question on quant topics. This event will help the students to know about relation between quant and logical reasoning. This will increase their mental ability to solve different kind of mathematical and logical problems asked to be solved in various competitive exams. The main objectives of the event are: · To enhance their knowledge to solve any question of this topic with tricks and minimum calculations. · To solve questions based on various quant topics on a regular basis and try using the different formulas to crack the solution for each question in an even shorter time span. · To help students understand the area of interest and strengths better. full_content: Dear Aspirants, Professional Enhancement means expanding your ability to perform a particular task or progressing in your career by upgrading your skills. No matter the field, skill enhancement is a prerequisite for a successful career. Every industry — from fashion to education — evolves with time, and as a result, our existing skills may become outdated, leading to limited or no professional growth. A person with the right blend of functional, technical, and interpersonal skills is always preferred in a professional environment compared to someone lacking these attributes. Therefore, opportunities to enhance your skills should never be missed. Centre for Professional Enhancement presents Skill Development Courses (SDC) and Summer Internship Courses beyond classroom hours for all students to gain industry-relevant skills that are highly beneficial during placements and job interviews, thereby enhancing employability. These courses not only help students upgrade their skills but also provide certificates (based on evaluation) that can strengthen their resumes. The courses are carefully designed to match current industry requirements and help students achieve their career goals. With a wide range of options available, students can select courses according to their interests and requirements. To enroll in these Skill Development and Summer Internship Courses, students are required to complete the payment process through the enrollment link provided below by 25th May 2026. The course timetable will be reflected on UMS before the commencement of classes. full_content: Centre for Professional Enhancement in collaboration with Division of Residential Services is going to conduct “Mind the Mindset – A Group Discussion Workshop on Responsibility, Ethics, Respect, and the Impact of Gen Z Culture”. The workshop aims to create a balanced platform where students can analyse modern challenges, understand diverse perspectives, and develop thoughtful approaches toward responsible personal and professional conduct in today’s rapidly changing society. To analyse real-life situations involving ethical dilemmas, lack of responsibility, and respect in contemporary student culture through structured group discussions. ? To evaluate the impact of social media trends and Gen Z behavioural patterns on interpersonal relationships, communication, and societal values. ? To develop constructive solutions and responsible perspectives to address social and ethical challenges in academic and professional environments. full_content: Under the aegis of the Centre for Professional Enhancement, Club “Verbal Juggernauts” of Mittal School of Business is organizing “Verbal Combat – A Competitive Group Discussion Event”. The event will provide students to experience the dynamics of a professional Group Discussion settings. The event will encourage participants to improve their verbal communication, problem-solving abilities, confidence, and teamwork skills in a competitive environment. Students will be assessed on various aspects including communication effectiveness, confidence, analytical thinking, teamwork, leadership qualities, and their ability to express and defend their viewpoints respectfully during the discussion. It will also equip students with the skills required for professional and corporate interactions by strengthening their communication, teamwork, and interpersonal abilities. The main objectives of the event are: · To strengthen professional communication abilities, including clear expression of thoughts, attentive listening, and confident presentation of ideas in a formal discussion environment. · To familiarize students with placement-style Group Discussions by providing practical exposure to real corporate recruitment scenarios. · To develop self-confidence and improve participants’ ability to present, justify, and defend their opinions effectively during discussions. Target audience: The students of all Schools of Lovely Professional University will participate in the event. full_content: Dear Students, Placement is the ultimate objective for every student joining a degree program at LPU. That is why we place prime importance on student placements and therefore invest maximum efforts in this direction, extending all possible support in your placement-related endeavors. Each semester of your program includes certain courses that are critically important for placements. Lack of preparedness in such courses can subsequently lead to issues in securing good opportunities. After a thorough analysis of your academic performance for term 1, it has been observed that for some students of 1st year CSE programmes (list of students attached), grades in Python Programming (INT108), a course highly important for effective placement opportunities is not upto the mark. To address this, a specialized 6week Summer Placement Readiness and Employability Enhancement Programme (SPR101) (tentatively from 15 June to 25 July 2026) has been designed specifically for these students without any fee (students joining in offline mode shall only be required to pay hostel fee). It is mandatory for these students to attend this programme. However, students may choose either of the two options: Supervised OnCampus Learning (Offline Mode) – preferred, with faculty mentorship and guided practice. Learning through Virtual Platforms (Online Mode) – online mode via suggested platforms (Infosys Springboard, Udemy, Harvard University course, etc.) along with mandatory CodeTantra assignments. Supervised OnCampus Learning (Offline Mode) Learning through Virtual Platforms(Online Mode) 2hrs daily class and 3hrs programming practice class, five days a week (Monday-Friday) Online course to be completed on platform as allocated by University. Mandatory physical attendance Daily doubt clearing session in evening & weekly progress check with mentor Mandatory Daily 08 programming problems on CodeTantra platform after class Mandatory Daily 08 programming problems on CodeTantra platform Weekly status check: 40 problems covered during the week. Saturday and Sunday will serve as additional days for completing the assigned problems. Weekly status check: 40 problems covered during the week. Saturday and Sunday will serve as additional days for completing the assigned problems. Weekly progress (described above) for 6 weeks contributes 30% to final grade for SPR101 Weekly progress (described above) contributes for 6 weeks 30% to final grade for SPR101 Final evaluation test after completion of course (offline, in University when it reopens) Final evaluation test after completion of course (offline, in University when it reopens) Each student is required to submit his/her preference for the online or offline mode through the link shared in my message. Submit your preference latest by 25 May 2026. Weekly problems are mandatory. Weekly problems carry 30% weightage and the final test to be conducted in University in offline mode carries 70% weightage. The students shall be provided necessary reading material and video lectures for immediate assistance. The final evaluation test is mandatory for all students and shall be conducted in offline mode when the University reopens. The grade obtained in SPR101 shall be considered for Grade Upgradation in the course Python Programming (INT108). In case the student’s performance in the exam is not satisfactory, the student may be restricted from future placement activities. In case of any clarification, or assistance related to the SPR101 Summer Placement Readiness Programme, students may raise an RMS through: UMS Dashboard -> RMS -> Master Category -> Placement (Career Services) -> SPR101 Summer Placement Readiness Programme Attachment: 1 List of Students.xls Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Academic Affairs *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

full_content: All students appearing in BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) mode Practical Examination scheduled from 14th May 2026 onwards are required to strictly follow the guidelines and adhere to the instructions mentioned below: 1. All students must report 30 minutes before the start of exam. Timely arrival is essential to begin the exam without disruptions and to resolve any technical issues. Latecomers will not be compensated for any delays due to technical issues. a. For example, if your test is scheduled for 09:30 A.M., you must report by 09:00 A.M. b. If your test is scheduled for 01:30 P.M., you must report by 01:00 P.M. 2. The total duration of the exam is 3 hours: a. The first 15 minutes are allocated for writing the question on the sheet. b. The next 30 minutes are for writing the solution on the sheet. c. The following 40 minutes are for implementation. d. An additional 15 minutes are allotted to handle any technical issues. e. After the execution viva of the student will be conducted. 3. All students must carry a valid University identity card for verification purposes. 4.Bring a fully functional laptop along with its charger. Ensure that your laptop is either fully charged or remains plugged in throughout the test. 5. Use only official LPU networks such as LPU Wireless, LPU Block-34, LPU Block-26, etc. Use of personal hotspots or any unauthorized networks is strictly prohibited. 6. Install the latest version of Exam browser(Neo browser, CodeTanta, EduCode etc.) before the exam. Using outdated versions may lead to compatibility issues. Ensure that the browser is functioning properly on your laptop at least one day before the test. 7. Do not open any other windows or applications during the test. Stay active on the test screen only, failing which may lead to premature termination of test. 8. No background applications should run except essential system processes. AI tools(Like ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Script etc.), screen-sharing software, and remote access tools are strictly prohibited, and shall lead to termination of the exam. 9. A mandatory mock test is assigned to all students starting 13th May 2026. Every student must attempt it before the actual exam. 10 .If you face issues with Browser, create a separate user account on your laptop without any additional applications installed to ensure smooth functioning. Ensure that the user account is functioning properly by attempting the mock test available in your account. 11 .The evaluation criteria for the assessment are as follows: The assessment will be conducted through three components with the following weightage: Written (40%), Execution (20%), and Viva (40%). The marks obtained in the execution component will be considered as they are, without any proration. 12. The execution consists of two sections(Total 30 marks): a.Section 1: 2 coding questions - (10 marks each) b. Section 2: 10 multiple-choice questions(MCQs) - (1 mark each) c. Section 2 can only be accessed after submitting Section 1. Once submitted, Section 1 will be locked. d. There is no negative marking. e. As the weightage is 20%, the execution marks (out of 30) will be converted to 20 marks. For example, if you score 24 out of 30, it will be converted to 16 out of 20. 13. Students are not allowed to leave the room during the test. Washroom breaks are strictly not permitted. 14. Mobile phones, bags, and other personal belongings, including smart gadgets, wireless earphones, smart glasses etc., are strictly prohibited inside the exam room. Only your laptop, charger and ID card are allowed. 15. An access key will be provided for each test and will be entered by the invigilator on your laptop. 16. Disable browser pop-ups before the test to avoid distractions. 17. Clear your browser cache and cookies before starting the test to prevent technical issues. 18. Do not use any wireless devices (headphones, earbuds, smart watch, smart glasses etc) during the test. 19. Strict action will be taken against students found using AI tools, DevTools, WhatsApp, Instagram, or any unauthorized application in the background. Offenders will receive zero marks. Excuses such as “It’s someone else’s laptop” or “The app was installed but not running” will not be accepted. Students are responsible for complying with all guidelines. Violations may result in exam cancellation and disciplinary action. Any form of cheating or unfair means will result in strict action, including reporting under UMC (Unfair Means Case). 20. Disable unnecessary startup applications in Windows settings before the test. 21. All students must fill out and submit an undertaking to their respective faculty members before the test. A hard copy will be provided during the exam. Failure to submit it will result in assessment cancellation. 22. No queries will be entertained after 3 hours, regardless of the situation. If you face any issues, discuss them with the assigned neutral faculty member, and ensure they are resolved within 3 hours only. 23. For the online assessment, only the last submitted code will be evaluated. 24. Important for all Students: It is important to reiterate that if anyone is found Involved in any act that amounts to “Unfair Means Case”, then his/her university scholarship shall stand cancelled for rest of the programme duration along with a penal action as per university regulations. Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Examination *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

full_content: All students appearing in BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) mode Practical Examination scheduled from 14th May 2026 onwards are required to strictly follow the guidelines and adhere to the instructions mentioned below: 1. All students must report 30 minutes before the start of exam. Timely arrival is essential to begin the exam without disruptions and to resolve any technical issues. Latecomers will not be compensated for any delays due to technical issues. a. For example, if your test is scheduled for 09:30 A.M., you must report by 09:00 A.M. b. If your test is scheduled for 01:30 P.M., you must report by 01:00 P.M. 2. The total duration of the exam is 3 hours: a. The first 15 minutes are allocated for writing the question on the sheet. b. The next 30 minutes are for writing the solution on the sheet. c. The following 40 minutes are for implementation. d. An additional 15 minutes are allotted to handle any technical issues. e. After the execution viva of the student will be conducted. 3. All students must carry a valid University identity card for verification purposes. 4.Bring a fully functional laptop along with its charger. Ensure that your laptop is either fully charged or remains plugged in throughout the test. 5. Use only official LPU networks such as LPU Wireless, LPU Block-34, LPU Block-26, etc. Use of personal hotspots or any unauthorized networks is strictly prohibited. 6. Install the latest version of Exam browser(Neo browser, CodeTanta, EduCode etc.) before the exam. Using outdated versions may lead to compatibility issues. Ensure that the browser is functioning properly on your laptop at least one day before the test. 7. Do not open any other windows or applications during the test. Stay active on the test screen only, failing which may lead to premature termination of test. 8. No background applications should run except essential system processes. AI tools(Like ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Script etc.), screen-sharing software, and remote access tools are strictly prohibited, and shall lead to termination of the exam. 9. A mandatory mock test is assigned to all students starting 13th May 2026. Every student must attempt it before the actual exam. 10 .If you face issues with Browser, create a separate user account on your laptop without any additional applications installed to ensure smooth functioning. Ensure that the user account is functioning properly by attempting the mock test available in your account. 11 .The evaluation criteria for the assessment are as follows: The assessment will be conducted through three components with the following weightage: Written (40%), Execution (20%), and Viva (40%). The marks obtained in the execution component will be considered as they are, without any proration. 12. The execution consists of two sections(Total 30 marks): a.Section 1: 2 coding questions - (10 marks each) b. Section 2: 10 multiple-choice questions(MCQs) - (1 mark each) c. Section 2 can only be accessed after submitting Section 1. Once submitted, Section 1 will be locked. d. There is no negative marking. e. As the weightage is 20%, the execution marks (out of 30) will be converted to 20 marks. For example, if you score 24 out of 30, it will be converted to 16 out of 20. 13. Students are not allowed to leave the room during the test. Washroom breaks are strictly not permitted. 14. Mobile phones, bags, and other personal belongings, including smart gadgets, wireless earphones, smart glasses etc., are strictly prohibited inside the exam room. Only your laptop, charger and ID card are allowed. 15. An access key will be provided for each test and will be entered by the invigilator on your laptop. 16. Disable browser pop-ups before the test to avoid distractions. 17. Clear your browser cache and cookies before starting the test to prevent technical issues. 18. Do not use any wireless devices (headphones, earbuds, smart watch, smart glasses etc) during the test. 19. Strict action will be taken against students found using AI tools, DevTools, WhatsApp, Instagram, or any unauthorized application in the background. Offenders will receive zero marks. Excuses such as “It’s someone else’s laptop” or “The app was installed but not running” will not be accepted. Students are responsible for complying with all guidelines. Violations may result in exam cancellation and disciplinary action. Any form of cheating or unfair means will result in strict action, including reporting under UMC (Unfair Means Case). 20. Disable unnecessary startup applications in Windows settings before the test. 21. All students must fill out and submit an undertaking to their respective faculty members before the test. A hard copy will be provided during the exam. Failure to submit it will result in assessment cancellation. 22. No queries will be entertained after 3 hours, regardless of the situation. If you face any issues, discuss them with the assigned neutral faculty member, and ensure they are resolved within 3 hours only. 23. For the online assessment, only the last submitted code will be evaluated. 24. Important for all Students: It is important to reiterate that if anyone is found Involved in any act that amounts to “Unfair Means Case”, then his/her university scholarship shall stand cancelled for rest of the programme duration along with a penal action as per university regulations. Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Examination *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

full_content: INVITED POPULAR TALK: Subatomic Physics in Service of Mankind By Professor Raghunath Sahoo, FNASc, FInstP Institute Chair Professor, Indian Institute of Technology Indore Venue: 55A-502, Time: 4-5 PM Date: 11 May, 2026, Monday About the Speaker : Prof. Raghunath Sahoo is a distinguished physicist working in the field of high-energy nuclear physics with more than 25 years of research experience at leading international laboratories including CERN, Geneva and Brookhaven National Laboratory, USA. He is an active CERN-ALICE-India member and one of the laureates of the prestigious Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics 2025. He is an Institute Chair Professor at IIT Indore and has received numerous recognitions including: CERN Scientific Associate (2021–2022) Excellence in Research Award 2024, IIT Indore INSA Associate Fellow 2024 Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences India (NASI) Fellow of the Institute of Physics, United Kingdom His book on Relativistic Kinematics: A Journey in Spacetime published by Springer (2025) is widely used by the experimental high-energy nuclear physics community. Prof. Sahoo has served as the Deputy spokesperson, Chairperson of the ALICE-STAR India Collaboration and Associate Dean of International Relations. full_content: Centre for Professional Enhancement in collaboration with School of Computer Science and Engineering is going to conduct “Reader’s Bliss: A Workshop on Sailing Across the Ocean of Reading”, a workshop event to guide today’s tech-savvy students to pick up old-fashioned reading habits as they surf on the tides of 21st century. full_content: This is to notify all Continuing students that they can now apply for a Change of Program using the online interface available at the following link: UMS Navigation -->Change of Program--> Request for Change of Program. However, the students should meticulously go through the guidelines (attached with this communication) before applying for the same. Timelines for change of Program:- Phase Processing Fee From To I Rs.1000/- 29th April, 2026 17th June, 2026 II Rs.3000/- 18th June, 2026 31st July, 2026 III Rs.5000/- 1st Aug, 2026 29th Aug, 2026 No program change option will be allowed after the last date i.e. 29th August, 2026 under any circumstances. Important Note:- 1. All students who apply for change of program shall be required to pay the “processing fee” online after submitting their request along with the parent’s consent letter/undertaking form. (Note: - The processing fee is non-refundable even if the change of program request of student is not approved by competent authorities) 2. The program of the student shall be changed for the notified students (approved cases) after the payment of change of program fee (Rs 4000/-) within the given timelines and the final approval of the competent authorities. 3. In case student fails to pay the fee as per timelines, the approval for the Change of Program shall stand cancelled and he/she would be required to continue in the ongoing program only. 4. No student will be allowed to transfer back to the old program after approval of Change of Program. 5. Due to course mapping if student is allocated additional courses to study to complete the requirements of the new program he/she will have to register the courses as backlog by paying the 1/10th of the tuition fee with scholarship plus 500/- (per course). 6. Only one chance is given to the students for change of program during the entire program duration, hence the students are advised to be very careful while availing this chance. 7. No benefit of missed CA or Attendance will be given to the student applying for change of program after start of classes. To avoid this, students are strongly advised to apply for the change of program before the start of the term. 8. The attendance shall be calculated from the date of registration of student in new program. Any queries from students can directly login an RMS following the below mentioned link: UMS Navigation---->Relationship Management System (RMS)---->Log Request Master category: Academics Category: Academics Sub Category: Change of Program Attachment: 1 Changes in Guidelines for Change of Program continuing FINAL updated.doc 2 COP Parent's consent letter.doc Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Examination *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

Participants will begin writing a story and then pass it on for others to continue and complete. Through this activity, they will practice adapting to new ideas, building coherent narratives, and improving vocabulary and fluency. The workshop will encourage quick thinking and teamwork in a fun environment, and will conclude with sharing and reflection on the creative outcomes. full_content: Under the aegis of the Centre for Professional Enhancement, Club "Mission Power Skills" of Mittal School of Business is going to conduct “JD Decode Challenge: A Competitive Event to Decode, Strategize and Deliver” an engaging and skill-driven competition designed to enhance students’ ability to analyze Job Descriptions (JDs) and translate them into structured, insightful presentations. The event aims to develop a recruiter’s mindset among students, enabling them to understand industry expectations and align their skills accordingly. JD Decode Challenge will strengthen analytical thinking, strategic understanding, communication skills, and presentation confidence. Through a competitive and time-bound task, participants will work in teams to decode assigned JDs, map required skills, and deliver a professional pitch covering company insights, role expectations, and preparation strategies. The main objectives of the event are: · To help students understand how to effectively read, interpret, and analyze Job Descriptions in real-world hiring scenarios. · To equip participants with the ability to identify key responsibilities, required skills, and expectations from a role. · To enhance awareness of industry requirements and guide students on how to prepare strategically for specific roles. Target audience: The students of all Schools of Lovely Professional University will participate in the event. full_content: As per the scheme of CSE/IT, all second-year students (2028 graduating batch) are required to undergo a mandatory 4–6 weeks summer training/internship after the completion of their 4th semester (2nd year of B.Tech). Eligible students will be divided into the following two categories, and must complete training accordingly: 1. Domain Technologies Students in this category must complete their training/internship in non-programming domains, such as: Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Generative AI, Cloud Computing, Full Stack Development (FSD), Database, Networks, Cyber Security, Data Science,etc. Students in this category may also opt for an internship, subject to prior approval from the Career Counselling Cell. 2. Core Technologies Students in this category must complete their training in programming languages only, as it is essential for Computer Science students to gain strong programming proficiency. Categorization Criteria Categorization (Domain/Core) will be based on academic performance (grades from 1st to 3rd semester). For lateral entry students, it will be based on 1st semester grades. The category allocation will be communicated separately. Special PEP (Professional Enhancement Program) Due to evolving hiring practices, companies are now assessing students as early as the 5th semester and offering internships after the 6th semester. To prepare students a selected group (from placement-registered students) will undergo Special PEP training. This training will be conducted offline on campus. Allocation in this input will be through a test followed by interview. Selected students must stay on campus during summer vacations. The list of shortlisted students will be shared separately. Competitive Programming/Data Structures and Algorithms, Professional Communication Skills will be taught during the training. A Mandatory Summer Training Project will be part of training program. Placement Preparedness Course A comprehensive, accessible training program for students who wish to strengthen their placement readiness skills while remaining on campus. Key Features: Selection Process: No entrance test required; open enrollment for all Students Mode: Paid Program Curriculum Focus: Core Programming Concepts + Data Structure and Algorithms Database Management Systems (DBMS) Computer Networks Professional Communication Skills Mandatory Project Additional Resources: Access to LMS (Learning Management System) Portal AI-Powered Mock Interview Platform Personalized feedback and performance analytics Category: Core Technologies Training / Internship Process: For detailed information Visit Website Link: https://tinyurl.com/csesummertraining2028 NOTE: You are advised not to enroll in any course without verifying your eligibility(CORE/DOMAIN) and getting the confirmation of the recommended courses from website. full_content: This is in reference to the Ph.D. State of the Art Seminar (SAS) evaluation which shall be tentatively scheduled from May 2026. The main aim of the Ph.D. State of the Art Seminar (SAS) evaluation is finalization of : a) Title of the proposed research work. b) Objectives of the proposed research work. c) Research methodology of the proposed research work. The research scholar must fulfill the following eligibility criteria for SAS registration: a. The research scholar must have cleared the course work or must be exempted for the same due to M. Phil. b. Term Registration must be completed at the time of registration c. Attendance criteria must be fulfilled as per university policy Note: Research scholars from the School of Agriculture who have cleared the first term of coursework may request for registration at: rdc.sas@lpu.co.in The research scholars must take the following three steps to register and appear for SAS evaluation. 1. Registration for SAS evaluation: All eligible research scholars are required to register for SAS evaluation through the following UMS path: Academics ---> Research and Development--> Registration of Upcoming Activity-->SAS Note: The interface for registration will remain active from 17th April 2026 to 13th May 2026. 2. Uploading of SAS Synopsis: All registered research scholars are required to upload their synopsis (prepared strictly according to the attached guidelines) through the following UMS path: Academics---> Research and Development--> Registration of Upcoming Activity-->SAS-->Click to Submit report. All the research scholars are required to completely register for SAS evaluation. The registration will only be considered as complete if the scholars will upload the synopsis followed by the verification of synopsis by their supervisors. Note: The link for uploading of SAS synopsis will remain active from 17th April 2026 to 13th May 2026. 3. Recommendation of SAS synopsis by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/ Administrative supervisor: Once the research scholar has uploaded their SAS synopsis for the evaluation, the same must be recommended by their respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor by visiting the following path: UMS navigation --->Division of Examination---> Department of Ph.D. Evaluations --->Ph.D. Seminar File Verification --->SAS. If the supervisor does not verify the synopsis of the scholar, it will be considered as rejected and the scholar will not be allowed to appear in the SAS evaluation. Note: The last date for the recommendation of the SAS synopsis by Supervisor/Co Supervisor/Administrative Supervisor 15th May 2026. Important Note: For Registration and Uploading of SAS synopsis: a) At the time of SAS registration, the research scholars should opt the domain for their SAS Seminar very carefully after consulting with their Supervisor/Co Supervisor/ Administrative Supervisor (if any) as they will be evaluated by the expert panel from the selected domain only. No request for change in domain shall be entertained afterwards. b) The SAS synopsis must be uploaded through UMS interface as per the prescribed timelines. No extension shall be given for registration for SAS beyond the last date. c) The registered scholars who wish to de-register themselves, may do so through a request application forwarded to Department of Ph.D. Evaluation duly recommended by supervisor no later than 13th May 2026, failing which the scholar will be marked absent during the SAS evaluation and will have to pay INR 5000/- as fee for registering in the next SAS. d) If a research scholar registers for the SAS evaluation but does not upload the synopsis by the stated last date or he/she is absent at the date of SAS seminar/evaluation then he/she shall be required to re-register for the next scheduled SAS evaluation with the applicability of fee of Rs. 5000/- subject to fulfilment of other eligibility criteria. He/ she shall only be allowed to appear in next scheduled SAS (scheduled tentatively from November 2026 onwards) only after the clearance of all pending dues. e) The research scholars must upload a single PDF file for SAS synopsis duly verified and signed by the respective supervisors strictly as per the attached guidelines (Guidelines for SAS) to complete the registration process or else their registration may be cancelled. f) File containing cropped signature of the supervisor shall not be considered for the evaluation. Scholars are advised to scan the page containing the signature of the supervisor and include it as a part of final PDF document to be uploaded. h) Research scholars are required to bring two hard copies of the Synopsis report, duly verified and signed by the respective Supervisor/Co-Supervisor/Administrative Supervisor (wherever applicable), at the time of evaluation. i) It is mandatory to submit one hard copy of the SAS report to CRDP (Block 38, Room No. 304), while the second copy must be retained by the scholar for reference by the panel members during the evaluation. j) File containing PDF of snapshots of pages is strictly prohibited and shall not be considered for evaluation. k) Research scholars should go through the attachment (Snapshots for using the SAS registration interface) before registration and uploading the SAS synopsis at the interface. m) The research scholar must bring their own laptop and projector cable (HDMI & VGA) for connecting the projector at the time of evaluation (mandatory). For Recommendation of SAS synopsis: 1. The research scholar must upload the SAS synopsis well-in-advance so that it can be recommended by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor within the stipulated timelines. 2. Supervisor must ensure that the research scholars upload the files within the stipulated timelines. In case, any of the eligible research scholars has query regarding SAS registration, the paths for submitting RMS requests are provided below: 1. For Registration/Uploading of SAS report, submit RMS by following the path: Student Services --> Relationship Management System --> Log Request --> Select Message Type (Enquiry) --> Select Category (Academic and Administrative issues) --> Select Department (Ph.D. - Research Degree Evaluation Cell) --> Sub Category: SAS. 2. For Supervisor / Co-supervisor submit RMS by following the path: UMS Navigation --> Relationship Management System --> Log Request --> Select Message Type (Enquiry) --> Select Category (Academic and Administrative issues) --> Select Department (Ph.D. - Center for Research Degree Programmes). full_content: Dear Staff/ Faculty/ Students It is our privilege to invite you to the Grand Finale of the Bharat Innovation Challenge 2025-26, to be held on 17th & 18th April 2026, at the campus of Lovely Professional University, Punjab. Recognised as India's Biggest Brain Marathon, the Bharat Innovation Challenge is a national initiative that empowers students aged 13–18 to develop AI-powered, real-world solutions. What began as a vision has evolved into a nationwide movement, engaging participants from 28 states, 500+ cities, and thousands of schools across India. The Grand Finale marks the culmination of this journey, bringing together the most promising young innovators from across the country. Finalist teams will showcase their ideas and prototypes before an esteemed panel of industry leaders, academicians, and domain experts, offering them a unique platform for recognition and growth. The Event Will Feature: 1. Innovation Expo showcasing student prototypes 2. Pitching sessions to jury from industry 3. Industry & expert interactions 4. Awards & recognition ceremony Participants will compete across multiple themes and categories, with top teams receiving cash prizes worth Rs. 14+ Lakh, further encouraging innovation and excellence. The Bharat Innovation Challenge is supported by a strong ecosystem of industry and knowledge partners, whose contributions play a vital role in mentoring participants and strengthening the overall impact of the initiative. We believe that your presence will add immense value to this celebration of innovation and will inspire the young minds who are shaping the future of our nation. We would be honoured to have you join us on this significant occasion. The formal invitation is attached herewith for your reference. For more queries, please contact Mr. Amritpal Singh Kalsi (98885-98735), Dr. Manoj Sindhwani (90415-93324), Mr. Rahul Vishwakarma (97795-45556). Attachment: 1 2026-04-16 - BIC - Invitation for Finale.pdf Uploaded By: Office of HOD Office of Admissions *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

Students are advised to register before the deadline to get help in their academics and clear pending (E/G) grade. full_content: This is in reference to the Ph.D. End Term Presentation (ETP) evaluation which shall be tentatively scheduled from June 2026 onwards (exact dates will be shared in due course of time). All the research scholars who have successfully completed their State-of-the-Art Seminar (SAS) evaluation are required to appear for End Term Presentation (ETP) biannually after successful completion of SAS. Aim of the End Term Presentation a. To present the action taken against the recommendations given by the Research Advisory Committee (RAC) in the previous evaluation. b. To present the work done or progress made since the last evaluation The research scholar must fulfill the following eligibility criteria for registration process: The eligibility criteria for registration for ETP 1 and ETP 2 a. Term Registration must be completed at the time of registration b. Attendance criteria must be fulfilled as per university policy The eligibility criteria for registration for ETP 3 and onwards a. Term Registration must be completed at the time of ETP registration b. Attendance criteria must be fulfilled as per university policy for that term. c. At least one research paper submitted/communicated in Scopus indexed journal required to register/appear in ETP3 evaluation. except for the scholars of Ph.D.-Hindi and Punjabi domain where research paper accepted/published in UGC indexed journal will be considered for evaluation. d. At least one research paper accepted/published in Scopus indexed journal required to register/appear in ETP4 and onwards evaluations except for the scholars of Ph.D.-Hindi and Punjabi domain where research paper accepted/published in UGC indexed journal will be considered for evaluation. e. In case the scholar has communicated/accepted/published a research/review article, the scholar is required to select the log request ID while registering for ETP evaluation. A log request can be generated through the supervisor’s UMS via following path: UMS Navigation --> Research and Development Cell --> Research and academic contributions --> Monthly status of research achievements/log request Note: All the scholars eligible for ETP 3 and above are required to register and upload the ETP report irrespective of their publication status. If the publication condition is not fulfilled, the scholar will not be allowed to appear in front of Research Advisory Committee rather and the case will be forwarded to Research Mentorship Committee (RMC) panel for guidance regarding research publications, for which a separate schedule will be shared with such scholars. Steps for ETP Registration: - The research scholars must complete the following steps to register for ETP evaluation. 1. Registration for ETP evaluation All eligible research scholars as per the attached list (List of research scholars eligible for ETP) are required to register for ETP evaluation through the following UMS path: Academics ---> Research and Development--> Registration of Upcoming Activity-->ETP Kindly watch the guided video on How to register for ETP by clicking on the following link- https://youtu.be/_IkzLlh69gE?si=jqU9-y8SIQahk81i Note: The interface for registration will remain active from 10th April 2026 to 6th May 2026 (snapshots for using the interface for registration is attached along with the announcement). 2. Uploading of ETP reports All registered research scholars are required to upload their files (prepared strictly according to the shared guidelines) through the following UMS path: Academics --> Research and Development--> Registration of Upcoming Activity-->ETP-->Click to Submit report. ETP reports will be considered only if submitted through the UMS interface. Submissions made through any other means, such as email or RMS, will not be accepted. Therefore, all scholars must ensure that their reports are uploaded through the online interface. Note: The link for uploading of ETP report will remain active from 10th April 2026 to 6th May 2026 3. Selection of ETP Evaluation Slot Research scholars are required to select their preferred week for the upcoming ETP evaluation through the UMS interface after uploading the ETP report. The scholars can follow the below mentioned Path for selecting the slots: Academics --> Research and Development--> Registration of Upcoming Activity--> Click to Select the ETP Evaluation Slot --> Click to select the ETP evaluation slot The selected slot will be final and cannot be changed under any circumstances. Scholars must ensure their availability as per the allotted schedule. Slot modification will be permitted only in case of a university-declared event or holiday. Note:- The scheduled slots are applicable only for RAC evaluation, and availability is limited for each domain; therefore, scholars are advised to book their slots at the earliest to secure their preferred schedule. If a scholar fails to select a slot within the stipulated timeline, the Department of Ph.D. Evaluation will automatically assign a slot based on availability. 4. Recommendation of ETP Report by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/ Administrative supervisor: Once the research scholar has uploaded their ETP report for the evaluation, the same must be recommended by their respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor by visiting the following path UMS navigation -->Division of Examination--> Department of Ph.D. Evaluation -->Ph.D. Seminar File Verification -->ETP Note: The last date for the recommendation of the ETP report by Supervisor/Co-Supervisor/Administrative Supervisor is 11th May 2026. If the supervisor does not verify the report of the scholar, it will be considered rejected and the scholar will not be allowed to appear in the ETP evaluation. Important Note: a) The research scholars must upload a single PDF file for end term report duly verified and signed by the respective supervisors strictly as per the attached guidelines (Guidelines for ETP) to complete the registration process or else their registration may be cancelled. b) File containing cropped signature of the supervisor shall not be considered for the evaluation. Scholars are advised to scan the page containing the signature of the supervisor and include it as a part of final PDF document to be uploaded. c) The ETP report must be uploaded through UMS interface as per the prescribed timelines. No extension shall be given for registration for ETP beyond the last date. d) Research scholars are required to bring two hard copies of the ETP report, duly verified and signed by the respective Supervisor/Co-Supervisor/Administrative Supervisor (wherever applicable), at the time of evaluation. e) It is mandatory to submit one hard copy of the ETP report to CRDP (Block 38, Room No. 304), while the second copy must be retained by the scholar for reference by the panel members during the evaluation. f) Cropped or digital signatures on the hard copy of ETP report will not be considered. g) File containing PDF of snapshots of pages is strictly prohibited and shall not be considered for evaluation. h) Research scholars should go through the attachment (Snapshots for using the ETP registration interface) before registration and uploading the ETP reports at the interface. i) As per the current guidelines, the research scholars who are eligible for ETP evaluation as per the attached list but do not complete the registration process/appear for the evaluation after registration will be marked absent for the ETP evaluation, and the result of the evaluation will stand as "Unsatisfactory". j) The research scholar must have a laptop and bring their own projector cable (HDMI to HDMI / HDMI to VGA) for connecting the projector at the time of evaluation (mandatory). k) The slot booking is not applicable for Research Mentorship committee (RMC) evaluation For Recommendation of the End Term Presentation Report: 1. The research scholar must upload the ETP report well-in-advance so that it can be recommended by the respective Supervisor/Co-supervisor/Administrative supervisor within the stipulated timelines and as per guidelines. 2.Supervisor must ensure that the research scholars upload the files within the stipulated timelines. In case any of the eligible research scholars has query regarding the following issues, the paths for submitting RMS requests are provided below: 1. For Registration/Uploading of ETP report, submit RMS by following the path: UMS Navigation --> Relationship Management System --> Log Request --> Select Message Type (Enquiry) --> Select Category (Academic and administrative issues) --> Select Department (Ph.D. - Research Degree Evaluation Cell) --> Sub Category: ETP. 2. For Supervisor / Co-supervisor / Extension / Term off/ document/fees, submit RMS by following the path: UMS Navigation --> Relationship Management System --> Log Request --> Select Message Type (Enquiry) --> Select Category (Academic and Administrative issues) --> Select Department (Ph.D. - Center for Research Degree Programmes). Attachment: 1 Snapshots for using the ETP registration interface.pdf 2 Guidelines for ETP Report 2026.pdf 3 List of Eligible Scholars for End Term Presentation May June 2026.xls Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Examination *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature
title: Instructions for Ph.D. Scholars and Supervisors Regarding Registration for End Term Presentation. : LPU/10.2/ANN(EXAM)/2024/023(23.4)(Vol-7)/IC/260410/0020 (4/10/2026)

full_content: This is for the information of all faculty members supervising the students registered in project, dissertation and similar courses (Annexure-I) that in order to be eligible for the Final End Term Presentation (ETP) viva, each student registered in such courses need to fulfil the following points as per the specified timelines mentioned in Annexure-III (Attached). 1. Uploading the soft copy of final report. All students need to prepare the final report of their research/ project work as per the guidelines attached (in Annexure-II) and upload the soft copy of the same in four parts i.e., PDF File-1, PDF File-2, PDF File-3 and PDF file-4 (details of pdf files are given in Table 1) via their UMS as per the timelines mentioned in Annexure-III by visiting the following path: UMS Navigation-->LMS-->Upload Research Project/Internship Certificate details-->Upload Research Project Report/Internship Certificate --->Project/Dissertation Table 1- Contents of each PDF file (size should be less than 5 MBs) PDF File 1* PDF File 2 PDF File 3 PDF File 4 (Applicable only for final stage Master Dissertation) Students need to upload their Complete Project/ research Report as PDF File 1. Students need to upload "only Content Report" which is without any student identification Information (e.g. Student's Name, Reg. Number or Title Page) as PDF File 2. Plagiarism Report is to be uploaded for Standalone Project(s), Capstone Project-II, Dissertation-II or Dissertation- III (As per Annexure-I). Allowed Plagiarism limit shall be as per the Policy which has been described under the following link available on UMS: https://www.lpu.in/academics/pdf/code-of-ethics.pdf . Also, AI plagiarism check will be applied so students should refrain from using AI. Student need to submit graphical abstract from Thesis/Dissertation work at Master's Level) Please ensure that PDF File 1 contains student as well as supervisor signatures on the declaration certificates before uploading the same on the UMS interface. Important Note- 1. It is advised that the student(s) must ensure timely uploading of their final report before the last date of submission so that the supervisors get sufficient time to approve or to get the modifications suggested by them incorporated in the final report before final submission of the hard copy of the report in the respective administrative officer (A.O.) office by the students. 2.In Extreme cases if the final report is not ready and requires more time, student can request for an extension of maximum 60 days with a fee of Rupees 1000/- in 30-310 by filling the hard copy Extension form. 3.The guidelines (Annexure-II) attached with this announcement for the preparation of the final reports are suggestive and can vary as per the nature and amount of the work done. 4.Respective supervisors must ensure that the reports submitted by the students get approved on or before the last date of submission as specified in Annexure-III. 2. Uploading the detail of the Research Publication/ Patent on UMS (if any): In case student/ student group has a research publication (at least acceptance proof)/Patent (submission proof) all students in a specific Project group need to fill the details of the Research Publications/Patent as per the timelines mentioned in Annexure-III by visiting the following UMS path: UMS Navigation-->LMS-->Upload Research Project/Internship Certificate details--->Upload Research Project Publication/Patent details The above interface would require a log request ID which can be generated by respective Supervisor via the following UMS path: UMS Navigation-->Division of Research and Development-->Research and Academic Contributions--->Log Request Note- It is mandatory to have the research publication/Patent affiliated with Lovely Professional University otherwise the student would not be eligible for the Final ETP viva-voce. 3. Online Report Recommendation from Supervisor: The soft copy of the final report uploaded by each student should be recommended by the supervisor in order to be eligible for the final ETP viva. In case report is not recommended by supervisor then final ETP viva for the student(s) shall not be conducted. 4. Submission of hard copy of the final report in the respective administrative office (A.O. Office) Once the respective supervisors have recommended the soft copy of the report submitted by the students, two hard copies, either spiral or hard bound (As per Annexure-I) of the same duly verified and signed by the respective supervisor must be submitted by the students in respective A.O. office as per timelines specified in Annexure-III. While submitting the hardcopy of project report the AOs must write the E-Receipt Number, sign and put their UID along with the University stamp on hardcopies carried by the student. One Signed and stamped copy of the report should be returned to the student and the same must be carried by the student at the time of ETP viva. Respective School AO’s can generate an online report submission number via the following UMS path. UMS Navigation-- >Administrative Task-->Report Submission Important Points: 1. For students working in groups, any one member of the group can make the submission in AO office and it will be considered for all. Whereas, the supervisor must recommend the uploaded soft-copy via UMS interface for all students in-order to enable hard-copy submission for the whole group.2. In case a student fails to submit his/her final report as per the specified timelines, R grade shall be awarded.3. Reports will be accepted in AO offices latest by 17:00 hrs. as per the last dates mentioned in Annexure-III. In case of any query, faculty may log an RMS request using the below mentioned link: UMS Navigation---->Relationship Management System (RMS)--->Log Request Select Category: Examination Select Sub Category: Others Attachment: 1 Annexure I.xls 2 Annexure II.rar 3 Annexure III.pdf Uploaded By: Office of HOD Division of Examination *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

full_content: The Department of Food Technology and Nutrition proposes to organize a HACCP Training Program for industry professionals, research scholars, and students in the food science discipline, in collaboration with the Human Resource Development Center, Lovely Professional University. Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) serves as a cornerstone of food safety management, providing a systematic framework for identifying risks and ensuring safety across the entire food supply chain—from raw material selection to final distribution—while aligning with FSSAI guidelines for enhanced hygiene and quality standards. The program is also strategically integrated with continuous assessment components of courses such as FOT489 (Food Quality Safety Standards and Certification) and FOT312 (Food Quality Management), ensuring academic rigor and practical applicability. Seize this opportunity to elevate and future-proof your data analytics capabilities in agricultural research. The details of program appended below: Title Short Term course on Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) Course Outcome Participants will be able to: *Be aware about the food safety and to gain the comprehensive knowledge about HACCP *Be eligible for HACCP certification of the participants Develop and Implement a HACCP Plan *Develop skill to drive implementation of HACCP in the organization *Develop capabilities to audit food production systems, from start to end for food safety compliance *Improve Record-Keeping and Documentation Practices Enhance Problem-Solving and Risk Management Skills Enhance the ability of skilled manpower in food industry Resource Person (s) Dr. Hamid, Assistant Professor, School of Agriculture, LPU Program Schedule Refer Brochure Attached Participants Faculty Members and Scientists Research Scholars and Students Professionals & Person from Industry. Date April 13 to 18, 2026 Time 06:30 PM -08:30 PM Registration Link https://www.lpu.in/hrd Program Mode Online: LPU My Class Payment & Mode LPU Associate Faculty Research Scholar & Students: Rs-1050/- External Participants: Rs- 1250/- Online Payment or Cash to be deposited in Accounts Department Last Date of Registration April 10, 2026 Since there are limited seats, selection will be on a first come first served basis Looking forward to your active participation Attachment: 1 Brochure -CCT2216.pdf Uploaded By: Office of HOD Human Resource Development Center *This is computer generated notice, not requiring signature

full_content: Admissions-Wing is recruiting students for Part time (9 am to 5 pm/6 pm) as a student counsellor. The primary purpose is to utilize student's talent, zeal and enthusiasm positively for In-campus tasks like counselling through Walkin/telephonic, preparation of ID cards and handling files, inquiry feeding, dispatching prospectus in postal cell etc. in the Division. Nature of Job: 01. Conducting surveys and collecting information from students/parents in Department of digital engagement: Student will be responsible for conducting surveys and collecting information, writing posts/content. 02. Data Entry, Reception handling, Campus visits, survey/Feedback and Routing in Walk-in Admission Cell: Candidates will be responsible for data entry for new enquiries, taking surveys/feedback and routing the enquiries to the Counselor for further processing including campus visit for parents/students 03.Walk-in handling and follow-up with parents/students for Loan related queries. Personality Traits, Working Hours and Salary: . Candidate should possess good communication and interpersonal skills . Good teamwork and team member . Efficient handling of Procedures. . Good Information of LPU’s strengths, processes and interfaces. . Good knowledge of using computers/internet/social networking/office tools. Estimated number of days in a week is 6 and working hours will be 8/9 hrs which can be extended on a rotational basis depending upon the task allotted. . Monthly salary will be fixed at Rs. 15000 per month. Shortlisting and Academic Criteria: . Students enrolled in Under Graduate/ Post Graduate Degree (with no active backlogs and without any major indisciplinary case). · Students having any curriculum requirement/Placement activity/Classes/Training scheduled during the period of job (Between May to July) which is clashing with job timings (9 am to 5 pm/6 pm) need not to apply. Students will not be relieved or exempted for this purpose during the tenure of job. · Students will be relieved one day before the start of classes. However, they may apply for leave within the tenure of the job. Minimum CGPA --- 6 CGPA without active reappear or backlog Working Hours: 9 AM to 5/6 PM -Min 08 Hrs shift Selection Procedure: Online Test & Personal Interview Last Date for registrations: 15th April 2026 All interested candidates with CGPA greater than 6, must register through the below path by 15th April 2026. full_content: The Progress Akanksha Scholarship for Women in STEM 2026 supports women in India pursuing first-year undergraduate studies in computer science-related fields with renewable financial assistance of up to INR 1,50,000 per year based on need. It is open to Indian women students enrolled in eligible computing and STEM courses, with a family income limit of INR 5,00,000 and a minimum of 75% in Class XII. Link for apply Scholarship: (Create an account on the official Kaleidoscope application portal) https://apply.mykaleidoscope.com/program/ProgressAkanksha2026IN The Last date for the scholarship is 11-04-2026 Eligibility Criteria of Scholarship 1. Be a woman with Indian citizenship 2. Enrolled in the first year of under-graduation program (B.E/BTech) and major in Computer Science Engineering (CSE), Computer Science Information Technology (CSIT), or related courses 3. Aggregate marks secured in XII standard examination must be 75% or above 4. Family income must not exceed INR 5,00,000 Exclusions 1. Progress employees, board members and their families are not eligible 2. Students in graduate school are not eligible 3. For the purpose of this scholarship, STEM is defined as computer science, software engineering, IT and/or computer information systems Benefits: Up to INR 1,50,000 per year Essay Requirement: Applicants must submit a 500 to1000 word essay covering: 1. Your passion for STEM 2. How your interest in STEM began 3. Your future goals 4. How you have helped others through: . Volunteering . Mentorship . Community engagement . Especially STEM-related activities How to Apply? . Eligible candidates must complete and submit an online application, including: . One required essay. . Copy of 12th standard mark sheet. . Copy of Government ID/Aadhaar Card. . University admission letter. . Proof of family income (Income Certificate, BPL card, or similar). . Resume/CV. The detailed guidelines for applying for this scholarship scheme can be checked from the following UMS link available in your UMS login of students: UMS Navigation------->Scholarship Management System------->Scholarship Policies-------->Session 2025-26--------> Akanksha Scholarship for Women in STEM All the eligible students have to submit their above-mentioned documents at Building No. 32, Room No.103(B), and Window No. 4. For Submission of documents, students must book time slots via the following UMS path: UMS Navigation -------> Scholarship Management System -------> Apply for Outer Agency Scholarship. Documents shall be received for verification by the Department of SSIV only in the booked time slots. In case of any query, you can contact Mr. Anil Dhawan, Deputy Registrar, Department of SSIV on RMS link: UMS Navigation – RMS – External Agency Scholarships and Credit Card Schemes – State Scholarship Information & Verification – Verification and Eligibility Criteria/Process of External Agencies Scholarship Schemes of All States (Govt./Pvt.) or contact us on 01824-444378. full_content: Continuous Assessment (CA) constitutes an integral component of the academic evaluation process, ensuring continuous learning and timely assessment of student progress. As per the University curriculum, there are certain course codes in which all CA components are mandatory. In such courses, students are required to appear in all scheduled CAs, and the marks obtained are considered in the final evaluation. To support the students who could not perform well in earlier CAs or were absent in any CA, the University is providing an opportunity through CA Recoup, which shall be applicable to all students of the regular term enrolled in courses where all CA components are compulsory. Application Process: 1. Students are required to apply through the Google Form link provided: https://forms.gle/Qcm7gXZt7vYx8sVZ8 All required details must be filled carefully and correctly. 2. Last date to apply: 10 April 2026. No applications shall be accepted after the deadline. 3. Students applying for multiple course codes must fill the form separately for each course. Important Points to note: 1. Only those students who apply through the official link shall be eligible for CA Recoup. 2. The Recoup CA marks (only if higher than previous attempted CA marks) shall be considered for the final CA calculation. 3. The CA Recoup shall be conducted in the class by the concerned faculty. 4. The last date to conduct CA Recoup is 30-04-2026. 5. Details such as syllabus, actual date of conduct, type of CA shall be communicated by the concerned faculty. 6. Recoup CA shall be planned in additional lectures and may be scheduled on Saturdays also (Except second Saturdays). 7. Recoup CA shall be applicable only for some selected Academic Tasks for the course codes as per the Annexure attached. In case of any query, you may visit the Division of Examination, 30-310, Cabin- 1.
